about: UK NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework 4.0: the 41 contributing outcomes under 4 objectives and 14 principles, assessed against what SecuRAX demonstrably does. CAF is outcome-based: indicators inform expert judgement, they are not a checklist.

source.title: NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF) 4.0
source.issued: NCSC, 2025 (Crown copyright; Open Government Licence v3.0)
source.caveat: Outcome IDs and short titles only; status is our own judgement against the indicators of good practice. Not an official CAF assessment.

items.title: Board direction
items.note: The board's own direction and accountability.

items.title: Roles and responsibilities
items.note: Gateway roles and a named owner per model; people's security roles are the organisation's.
items.next: Owner field on every control and KRI in the cockpit.

items.title: Decision-making
items.note: The cockpit puts red and amber items first, with the next action; decisions themselves are people's.
items.next: Record decisions taken from the cockpit with their reason.

items.title: Risk management process
items.note: Risk register with likelihood x impact, treatments, overdue lamp; the process and appetite are the organisation's.
items.next: Re-assess risk automatically when a new model or technology enters the inventory (CAF A2.a).

items.title: Understanding threat
items.note: CISA KEV and MITRE ATT&CK snapshots; attacks replayed through the real gateway.
items.next: Attacker-view threat model per estate component.

items.title: Assurance
items.note: Every claim needs a test or journey; maps fail CI when evidence goes stale; checksummed audit pack.

items.title: Asset management
items.note: Model inventory, including models served but not listed; the impact map covers every tracked file.
items.next: A full data and dependency inventory beyond models.

items.title: Supply chain
items.note: Third-party skills and code vetted, pinned and hashed; tampering withholds content.

items.title: Secure software development and support
items.note: Agent changes cannot pass by weakening tests; fitness budgets and SAST in CI.

items.title: Policy development
items.note: BFSI control library and packs; policies themselves are the organisation's.
items.next: Generate policy stubs from the applicable controls.

items.title: Policy implementation
items.note: Policies the gateway enforces (residency, identity) are proven on the real estate.
items.next: Map each policy to the enforcing control.

items.title: Identity, authentication and authorisation
items.note: Keys and OIDC, roles, MFA claim for privileged roles, lock-out; automated functions are identities too (CAF B2).

items.title: Device management
items.note: Endpoint and device management are the organisation's.

items.title: Privileged user management
items.note: MFA required for admin and auditor roles at the gateway.
items.next: Privileged session logging and periodic access review.

items.title: Identity and access management
items.note: Key add, rotate and revoke for the gateway.
items.next: Scheduled review of unused keys.

items.title: Understanding data
items.note: Data classes from what is found in a request; residency per class.
items.next: A data inventory with owners per data type (once-only, one owning store).

items.title: Data in transit
items.note: HTTPS edge with a private CA and TLS on every internal hop.

items.title: Stored data
items.note: AES-256 encrypted backups; wrong key and tampering refused.

items.title: Mobile data
items.next: Guidance and a check for phone storage of the Life OS (device encryption, screen lock).

items.title: Media and equipment sanitisation
items.note: Disposal of devices and media is the organisation's.

items.title: Secure by design
items.note: Rails, tool-call guard and kill switch restrict what automated decision-making can do (CAF B4.a).

items.title: Secure configuration
items.note: Configuration not code; config-clean and fitness checks fail CI on drift.

items.title: Secure management
items.note: Safe update with backup, health gate and rollback.
items.next: Separate admin path for estate management.

items.title: Vulnerability management
items.note: KEV-prioritised findings, container and IaC scans in CI.
items.next: An age/end-of-life check for pinned images, models and packages.

items.title: Resilience preparation
items.note: Failures injected with an SLO each; recovery measured.

items.title: Design for resilience
items.note: Self-healing estate and provider failover down to a local model.

items.title: Backups
items.note: Verified restore after losing the data volume; encrypted archives.

items.title: Cyber security culture
items.note: Culture is the organisation's.

items.title: Cyber security training
items.note: Training is the organisation's; the certification path (doc 46) supports a person's own.

items.title: Monitoring coverage
items.note: Gateway audit feeds the AI-SOC; estate health watched.
items.next: Wider sources (host, network) through the Wazuh organ.

items.title: Securing logs
items.note: Every gateway audit event carries the hash of the one before it; `./securax audit verify` names an edited, deleted or reordered event.
items.next: A daily signed anchor of the chain head kept outside the estate, so a whole rewritten run is also detectable.

items.title: Generating alerts
items.note: Outages detected, healed and alerted; andon pushes only on change.

items.title: Identifying security incidents
items.note: AI-SOC triage maps gateway events to ATT&CK/ATLAS.
items.next: Triage outcome tracking (true/false positive rate).

items.title: Monitoring tools and skills
items.note: People's monitoring skills are the organisation's.

items.title: Understanding behaviour and threat intelligence
items.note: KEV and ATT&CK snapshots offline.
items.next: Baseline of normal gateway behaviour and alerting on deviation.

items.title: Threat hunting
items.next: Documented, hypothesis-driven hunts over the audit log that become automated detections (CAF C2.a).

items.title: Response plan
items.note: One detection starts every applicable regulator's clock; drafts and filings tracked.

items.title: Response and recovery capability
items.note: Kill switch per model or all AI; restore proven.
items.next: Runbooks per incident type linked from the incident clock.

items.title: Testing and exercising
items.note: Game days with SLOs; every journey runs nightly.

items.title: Post-incident analysis
items.note: Blameless postmortems with five whys.
items.next: A postmortem journey on the real estate.

items.title: Driving improvements
items.note: Mechanisms tracked to done.
items.next: Monthly lessons digest across postmortems and game days.
